title: Navy contemporaries: Duane Tatro and length of service
summary: He recalls Duane Tatro and a future Kenton bass trombonist from the Great Lakes band and confirms about two years of service.

blocks.x: Did you have any colleagues from your high school or your naval tenure – not career – that turned up in the jazz field later on? Anybody that went on to make a name for him- or her- – himself, at that point?

When I was in boot camp, there was another tenor player. I tried out for the band when I was in boot camp. The Great Lakes Naval Station had an official jazz band. I tried out for it and didn‟t make it. The guy that was there, his name was Duane Tatro. Later on he became a composer and he wrote a lot of t.v. shows out here. I see him at the arrangers society meetings now. He didn‟t know me, but I knew who he was. A bass trombonist, who showed up in Kenton‟s band when I joined it, had been in that band then, although I didn‟t know him. Those are the only two that I remember.
We were talking about this horrible band that you were with in the Navy.
I think we‟ve said enough about that.
So your commitment was then two years as opposed to the four years, had you completed the officers training? How long was your . . . ?
I was in two years overall, including the college and the boot camp and the ship.
So if you joined in ‟44, then you were discharged in ‟46.
